title: Obligation record
description: One thing a regulation requires, in a form a test result can be mapped to. The text here is Sunflower's summary, never the instrument's own wording: a regulation is authoritative in its own language and a paraphrase that reads as a quotation is the fastest way to mislead a reader who cannot check.

id.description: instrument:citation, e.g. `ai-act:Art.15(4)`. Readable in a client deliverable without a key, and parseable with one split so a renderer can group by instrument without a join.

instrument.description: Closed. A new instrument is a decision about what this firm advises on, not a new string.

title.description: The article or clause heading, where the instrument gives one.

applies_from.description: The date this bites. Null only where the instrument sets no date of its own (a standard's clause, which binds when an organisation claims conformity rather than on a calendar). Required to be present so nobody has to infer it from the instrument's general entry into force, which is a different date and moved once already.

role.description: Who carries it. A client is usually a deployer and sometimes both, and an obligation mapped to the wrong role is advice to do somebody else's work.

system_class.description: Which classes this applies to. Keyed to what `tier/` can produce, so a test can assert the join closes.

summary.description: What it requires, in our own words, in one or two sentences.

evidence_expected.description: What a reviewer must be able to put in front of an auditor to say this is met. The field that makes a `review` obligation a handover rather than an excuse.

verifiable.description: What kind of evidence could EVER satisfy this, independent of any engagement. `test`: an adversarial run can produce it. `review`: no probe establishes it. `hybrid`: a test shows the control failed, only a review shows it exists.

status.description: Obligations are amended, never deleted: a report citing one must stay explainable after it changes.

source_url.description: Where this was read. For `ai-act`, `dora`, `cra` this must be EUR-Lex, so a client's own counsel can check it without asking us.

last_checked.description: These dates moved once, via the Digital Omnibus, and will move again. A record with no check date is a claim about a moving target with no indication of when it was true.

verification.description: Whether the citation and date were read off the linked official text, or carried from secondary sources. `unconfirmed` is publishable and must be visible; a wrong article number in a client deliverable is worse than a missing one.
